software-engineering/antigravity-for-fde.summary: Use Antigravity (or your AI coding environment) the way an FDE does: project context, prompts, checkpoints, and safe iteration on customer work.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: After you understand the FDE role and course flow, use Antigravity as your day-to-day partner for labs: project context, structured prompts, checkpoints, and the smallest fix when something breaks.

objectives: Open a project folder and run prompts against real files
Read checkpoint outcomes before moving to the next step
Escalate errors back to the AI with full context instead of guessing

software-engineering/git-docker-and-clou.summary: Version control, containers, and first cloud deploy patterns every FDE uses when handing work to a customer team.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Git keeps changes reviewable; Docker makes runs repeatable; cloud hosts (Render, AWS, and similar) host the POC and production URLs you will practice in Section 2.

objectives: Keep secrets out of Git and document them in .env.example
Explain what a container gives you over running on bare metal
Name the deploy surfaces this course uses for MVP and production

software-engineering/python-basics.summary: Learn variables, strings, lists, dictionaries, functions, loops and if statements, then see how a dictionary matches the JSON an API returns.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Learn variables, strings, lists, dictionaries, functions, loops and if statements, then see how a dictionary matches the JSON an API returns.

objectives: Store text, numbers and True/False values in variables, and format text with strings
Keep related values in a list or a dictionary, and read a value by its key
Write a function that returns a value, and use a loop with an if to count matching items

software-engineering/python-essentials-a.summary: Set up uv or venv, a clean project structure and Git, then read and write files with proper exception handling.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Set up uv or venv, a clean project structure and Git, then read and write files with proper exception handling.

objectives: Create a clean Python project folder and install packages without mixing with other projects
Read and write files safely, and catch errors instead of crashing
Save API keys in a .env file and keep them out of Git

software-engineering/data-structures-jso.summary: Turn nested JSON, CSV and text extracted from PDFs and Word files into clean tables.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Turn nested JSON, CSV and text extracted from PDFs and Word files into clean tables.

objectives: Pick the right Python structure (list, dict, and so on) for simple data jobs
Open JSON or CSV and turn nested data into a flat table you can work with
Clean missing or messy values so the table is ready to use

software-engineering/working-with-apis-r.summary: Call REST and LLM APIs without letting timeouts, rate limits or bad responses break the job.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Call REST and LLM APIs without letting timeouts, rate limits or bad responses break the job.

objectives: Call an API, check whether the response succeeded, and read the result
Handle timeouts, rate limits, and retries so a bad call does not stop the whole job
Write short logs so you can see what failed later

software-engineering/typing-pydantic-and.summary: Validate model output with Pydantic and run many calls concurrently without hitting rate limits.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Validate model output with Pydantic and run many calls concurrently without hitting rate limits.

objectives: Describe the shape of data you expect and reject replies that do not match
Run several API calls at once without starting too many at the same time
When a reply is invalid, ask again or fix it before you move on

software-engineering/fastapi-logging-and.summary: Wrap a model call in a FastAPI service, test it with mocked LLM calls and make failures debuggable.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Wrap a model call in a FastAPI service, test it with mocked LLM calls and make failures debuggable.

objectives: Wrap a model call behind a small web API with clear request and response shapes
Write tests that fake the model so you can check the API without spending tokens
Add logs that help you find why a request failed

software-engineering/fde-role-sdlc-and-h.summary: What a Forward Deployed Engineer does, the SDLC stages you will practise, and how Section 1 (foundations), Section 2 (customer delivery), and Section 3 (capstone) fit together.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This hour sets context before Python and FastAPI. You are learning how real customer engagements run—not building the Customer support ticketing system app yet.

sections.heading: What an FDE does
sections.body:
- Works with the customer on discovery, design, build, validation, deploy, and handover.
- Turns fuzzy requests into working software with clear acceptance checks.
- Uses AI tools and engineering discipline together—not only coding in isolation.

sections.heading: SDLC in this course
sections.body:
- **Discover & requirements** — Stages 3–4 (business, UI/UX).
- **Architecture** — Stage 5.
- **Build & test** — Stage 6.
- **Pilot & production** — Stages 7–8.
- **Operate & handover** — Stage 9.
- **Capstone** — Stage 10 applies everything on e-commerce projects.

objectives: Explain what an FDE does in plain language
Name the main SDLC phases you will practise from Stage 3 onward
Describe how Section 1 skills (Python and FastAPI) connect to the Customer support ticketing system customer flow and capstone

software-engineering/lab-0-python-basics.summary: Write one small Python script for a fruit shop that uses variables, strings, a list, a dictionary, functions, a loop and an if statement, then run it.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This lab builds the smallest useful Python script before any API work. No libraries and no database are needed.

objectives: Create variables, strings, a list and a dictionary.
Write functions that return values.
Run the script and confirm the output.

software-engineering/lab-fastapi-simple-.summary: Create a minimal FastAPI service with a welcome route and a /health route, then verify it with curl.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This lab builds the smallest useful HTTP API: a welcome route and a health check. No database is needed.

objectives: Start FastAPI with uvicorn locally.
Implement GET / and GET /health.
Prove both work in the browser and with curl.

software-engineering/lab-fastapi-validat.summary: Add Pydantic validation and pytest tests with FastAPI’s TestClient, so bad input returns 422 and core routes stay protected by tests.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This lab extends the API from Lab 1A. Invalid request bodies fail with a clear error, and automated tests check the routes without starting a server manually.

objectives: Add a Pydantic model so an invalid body returns 422.
Write pytest tests with TestClient for /health and the new route.
Fix a failing test with a small, targeted change.

software-engineering/assignment-harden-t.summary: Extend the Lab 1A and Lab 1B API with a small client that survives three failures (timeout, rate limit 429 and invalid JSON), then write a short note on the retry decisions.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: An API client that works only when everything goes right is not ready for real use. This assignment adds three routes that fail on purpose and a client that handles each failure.

sections.heading: Details
sections.body:
Deliverable: Updated main.py, client.py and note.md

Due: Before Session 2

sections.heading: Check-out question
sections.body: **Why should a 401 error never be retried?**

objectives: Add a timeout and a capped number of retries to an HTTP client.
Wait for the Retry-After time when a 429 response arrives.
Handle a reply that is not valid JSON without crashing.
Decide which failures are worth retrying and which are not.
checkpointQuestions: Why should a 401 error never be retried?
